headline: US wholesale inflation came in a touch cooler than expected, but bitcoin's brief bounce faded as tech stocks fell, and US bitcoin ETFs saw a sixth straight day of outflows.

market.asOf: Read about 16:21-16:24 UTC Fri 13 Nov (23:21 Bangkok; 11:21am ET) from CoinGecko's coin pages. Use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 28, Fear (alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index, read about 16:21 UTC); CoinMarketCap's own index was at 20, per KuCoin News.

stories.title: US wholesale inflation a touch cooler than expected; bitcoin's bounce fades
stories.summary: The October producer price index (PPI), which tracks inflation at the wholesale level, rose 0.3% on the month against 0.4% expected. Bitcoin edged up to about $69,500 right after the release, then gave the gain back as tech stocks fell, per CoinDesk. Markets still expect the Fed to raise rates in December, and higher rates tend to pull money away from risky assets like crypto.
points: Headline PPI: +0.3% on the month (0.4% expected), per Seoul Economic Daily, and 6.5% on the year, the highest yearly rate since November 2022, per ANI; The Coin Republic says 6.6% was expected.
Core PPI, without food and energy, rose 0.3% on the month, in line with forecasts, per The Coin Republic.
Bitcoin was back at about $68,700 by 10:24am ET as the Nasdaq fell 2%, with AMD down 9% and Nvidia down 3.3%, per CoinDesk.
The 10-year Treasury yield was 5.14% after the release, heading for its worst week since April 2025, per CoinDesk.
CME FedWatch odds of a December hike were 89.4% after the release, per Seoul Economic Daily.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $68,000-69,000 after slipping below its 200-week average
stories.summary: Bitcoin dropped early on Friday to $67,652, per CoinDesk, falling below its 200-week moving average of about $68,000, a long-term trend line many traders watch. Exchanges force-closed more than a billion dollars of leveraged bets, mostly bets on rising prices. CoinDesk notes bitcoin is down more than 21% this year after falling 6.3% in 2025, so it is on course for its first back-to-back losing years.
points: Friday's low depends on the source: $67,652 per CoinDesk; KuCoin News says briefly below $68,000, its lowest since 19 August.
Leveraged bets force-closed in 24 hours: $1.65B per CoinGlass data cited by KuCoin News; CoinCentral gave $1.47B earlier in the day.
To finish 2026 up, bitcoin would need to close the year above $87,500, per CoinDesk.
Average funding rates on perpetual futures turned negative for the first time in a month, per Glassnode via CoinDesk: more traders are paying to bet on falling prices.
Prices above were read around 11am ET; use the live prices on this page for the current level.

stories.title: Six straight days of ETF outflows; new SEC and CFTC nominees named
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin and ether funds both lost money for a sixth day in a row on Thursday, taking away a key source of steady buying. Separately, the White House sent the Senate four nominees for the SEC and CFTC, the two main US market regulators for crypto, including a replacement for Hester Peirce, who led the SEC's crypto task force.
points: Bitcoin ETFs had $284M of net outflows on 12 November, $204M of it from BlackRock's IBIT, per SoSoValue data reported by KuCoin News.
Ether ETFs lost $70.57M the same day, $62.01M of it from BlackRock's ETHA, per PANews.
SEC nominees: Steven Levine (Republican, to succeed Peirce) and Kristin Johnson (Democrat, a former CFTC commissioner), per The Block.
CFTC nominees: Nathan Anonick (Republican) and Matthew Rowland (Democrat), both of whom worked on the Clarity Act, per The Block.

briefs.title: South Korea lets exchanges freeze on suspected hacks
briefs.summary: South Korea's Financial Services Commission will let exchanges pause deposits and withdrawals when they only suspect a hack, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Stablecoin supply shrinks fastest since 2022
briefs.summary: Stablecoin supply fell $14.2B in the 30 days to 9 November, the biggest drop since June 2022, per Glassnode data reported by crypto.news.
